title: Menus, Tabs, Topbar/Sidebar Polish — Including the Accessibility Pass
priority_note: Second priority, per the owner's explicit ordering: chat, then menus/tabs, then games, then wildcard sites. Roadmap: 'Same file, different section (#topbar, sidebar icon rail, settings panels) — accessibility pass included, since this branch's own name (chore/daveai-a11y-source-truth) says that's an active goal.'
audit_status_note: A section-by-section bug audit of the live production source (vps/daveai-ui-v6.html, brain_llm.py, CSS, and infra scripts) produced 133 candidate findings; 83 were independently confirmed real. The other 50 are NOT confirmed-false — they are pending re-verification after an unrelated rate-limit interruption stopped that re-check pass partway through. Treat any finding not explicitly marked confirmation_status='confirmed' or 'verified-in-this-contract' below as unresolved, not cleared. No consolidated ledger of all 133 findings exists in this repository as of 2026-09-15; the items under known_findings here are only the ones specifically flagged for this phase.

summary: Same physical file as CT-001, different section: the topbar, sidebar icon rail, and settings panels. Includes a real accessibility pass — the branch this work happens on is literally named for accessibility/source-of-truth work, and nothing found so far confirms the monolith's nav has actually had one.
background: vps/daveai-ui-v6.html is one 12,920-line file; CT-001 covers its chat logic, this contract covers its navigation chrome and settings surfaces. Two specific, independently confirmed accessibility findings from the 2026-09-15 follow-up bug audit land squarely in this contract's scope: the primary sign-in form and the entire Settings modal (~23 toggles) lack accessible names for screen readers. A related, already-audited precedent exists in this same repo: a prior accessibility pass on the unrelated app/ (bolt.diy) stack found 17 separate accessibility gaps fanning out from just 4 shared primitives, several structurally unable to carry an aria-label at all — a useful pattern to check for here (a handful of shared components missing label plumbing, rather than 23 independent one-off mistakes), but that audit's specific findings do not apply to this file; they were about a different, disconnected codebase.

status_discipline.verified: You personally read the code, ran the command, or fetched the live response yourself in this session, and can quote the exact evidence.
status_discipline.reported: A document or another agent's proof artifact says so, and you have not independently re-checked it today.
status_discipline.rule: Never upgrade a 'reported' fact to a 'verified' claim without re-checking it yourself. Label every claim in your completion report as one or the other.

cross_phase_notes: Fix labeling/ARIA only. Do not change the sign-in form's or Settings modal's underlying functional/session logic here — that is CT-001's scope on the same elements. If a label fix requires restructuring markup in a way that could affect CT-001's functional work, coordinate rather than proceeding silently.

While auditing settings toggles, check whether any of them control the narrator-first routing gate, the approval/governance gating layer, or the manual agent-routing override described in CT-001's F-P1-02 (features present in current production but not in the older daveai-v7 split). If so, make sure the accessibility fix does not hide, rename, or reroute that control silently — flag it for whoever holds CT-001 rather than resolving ambiguity unilaterally.
Do not touch the games catalog or its rendering — that is CT-003's scope, even where a settings toggle or nav item happens to link to it.
steps: Confirm CT-000 and CT-001 are done (or at least that CT-001's changes to this file are merged) before establishing your own line-number baseline.
Read docs/DAVEAI_DEEP_AUDIT_ROADMAP_20260915.md §5 Phase 2 and §4.4 (for pattern reference only) in full.
Read this contract in full, including known_findings and cross_phase_notes.
Locate the topbar, sidebar icon rail, sign-in form, and Settings modal markup by reading the file directly — do not rely solely on the line hints above, which are non-exhaustive.

For each interactive control lacking an accessible name, add the appropriate fix (aria-label, aria-labelledby, or an associated <label for=...>) using standard WCAG technique choice: prefer a visible <label> where one can be shown, aria-label/aria-labelledby where a visible label is not appropriate for the design.
Verify keyboard operability alongside labeling — a control with a new accessible name but no keyboard path is still broken for the same users.
Test with at least one real screen reader or an automated accessibility checker (e.g. axe) against the live or locally-served page, not just a visual/code read.
Gather required_evidence for every fix before writing a completion report.
Check every definition_of_done line item against your own evidence before declaring any of them done.
required_evidence: For F-P2-01 and F-P2-02: the exact diff of changed lines (before/after) for every element given a new accessible name.
An automated accessibility scan (e.g. axe-core) output, before and after, showing the specific violations resolved.
A screen-reader (or accessibility-tree/read_page-equivalent) transcript demonstrating the sign-in form and at least a sample of Settings-modal toggles now announce a meaningful name.
A keyboard-only walkthrough (no mouse) demonstrating the sidebar/topbar/settings controls touched by this contract remain operable.
An exact count of toggles found in the Settings modal (confirm or correct the reported ~23 figure) and how many were fixed vs. remaining, with reasons for any left unfixed.
A restated definition_of_done checklist with each line marked done/blocked/not-attempted and an evidence pointer for every 'done' line.
reporting_requirements: State exact counts: how many of the sign-in form's controls and how many of the Settings modal's toggles were found, how many were fixed with evidence, and how many remain (with reasons).
Every item claimed fixed must cite a required_evidence artifact by file path or exact command+output, not a narrative description.
Never use a forbidden_claim_patterns phrase to describe this contract's outcome unless the exact proof command+output is quoted directly next to it.

If you find additional accessibility or nav bugs outside the sign-in form / Settings modal while working, record them (file + line + description) and hand them off rather than silently expanding scope.
definition_of_done: [ ] F-P2-01: the primary sign-in form's controls have accessible names, verified with an automated scan and a screen-reader/accessibility-tree transcript.
[ ] F-P2-02: every toggle in the Settings modal has an accessible name, verified the same way; the exact toggle count is confirmed (or corrected from ~23) and stated in the report.
[ ] Keyboard operability of every control touched is verified, not assumed.
[ ] No functional/session logic in the sign-in form or Settings modal was changed under cover of this contract.
[ ] No file outside this contract's scope list was modified, or every such change is explicitly disclosed with a reason.
[ ] Completion report uses verified/reported labeling per status_discipline, states exact counts per reporting_requirements, and contains no forbidden_claim_patterns phrase without adjacent proof.

failure_policy.if_blocked: Stop. Document exactly what is blocking you (e.g. cannot determine the intended visible label text for a given toggle) and why. Do not guess a label that misrepresents the control's function, silently skip it, or mark it done anyway.
failure_policy.if_partially_done: Report exact done/blocked/not-attempted counts against the sign-in form and each Settings-modal toggle. Partial completion is a legitimate, honest outcome — an inflated claim is not.

rollback_plan: Before installing any change to /var/www/agentic-website on the live VPS, snapshot the current file(s) to a timestamped backup directory, following the existing pattern in vps/patches/deploy-accessibility-contract-20260725.sh (backup → install → verify with sha256sum/curl → trap-based rollback to the backup on any verification failure). Labeling-only changes are low-risk but should still go through this pattern given the file is hand-deployed with no CI.
